$purpose: THE CLOSED VOCABULARY OF BOSS NAMES, plus what is durably known about each one.
1. A NAME NOT IN THIS FILE IS NOT A BOSS. The schedule's hardest rule is never to invent a name
-- a plausible wrong one is indistinguishable from a right one until the player travels
somewhere empty. Checking a candidate against this list makes that rule mechanical instead of
a matter of care. If a capture produces a name that is not here, it is a misread or a new
addition, and either way it needs confirming before it goes in the schedule.
2. IDENTIFY ONCE, NOT EVERY CAPTURE. Zone and kind come from the client's hover tooltip, which
costs the player one hover per boss. Recorded here, that cost is paid once per boss for good
Source: the map's Content Settings window, which lists every boss beside its icon WITH ITS NAME IN
TEXT -- read 2026-08-04 from a live client, patch 4.5.0. That one screen is the complete roster.
$whyThereIsNoModeHere: CONTEST MODE IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and this is the single most important thing about this file.
Mode belongs to the OCCURRENCE, not the boss. Two tooltips, same boss, same weekday, same time,
05/08 Wed 20:00   [Guild] Ramux -- Stillreach, Lv. 60, despawns after 50min
So a `mode` field on a boss would be wrong roughly half the time, and wrong in the direction that
costs a player their evening: a guildless player told a boss is open cannot enter, and a guild told
a boss is theirs finds it open to everyone.
- The HOURLY stream: from the SLOT TIME. 18:30 and 21:30 Pacific are guild every day and the
other five slots are peace. That is stable, it is already encoded as `mode` on those slots in
boss-schedule.json, and it needs no per-boss data at all.
- The ARCHBOSS stream: from the hover tooltip, per occurrence, onto a dated slot.
- NEVER from the badge in a screenshot. The overlay badge (shield = PvP, dove = peace) is real
and legible on the player's own monitor, and it does NOT survive capture -- tested 2026-08-06
and it failed. Screen capture arrives downsampled, so a 20px icon lands at ~11px and its corner
badge at three or four pixels. Zooming upscales blur.
$fields: name   -- exactly as the client prints it. The authority for spelling.
kind   -- boss | archboss | boonstone. Per-boss and stable, unlike mode.
zone   -- where it spawns, from the tooltip's second line. null means nobody has hovered it yet.
The player has to travel there, so a countdown naming the zone is worth more than one
level  -- monster level from the tooltip, null when unread.
Filling zone/level is incremental and optional: one hover per boss, and the schedule is useful
with them all null. Do not guess either. An absent zone is honest; a wrong one sends the player
$ascendedNote: Most bosses exist in a normal and an 'Ascended' form, listed separately in Content Settings and
treated here as separate entries because they are separate schedule icons. Porfos and Thuban have
no Ascended form in the roster as read. Do not synthesise 'Ascended X' for a boss that does not
$filterWarning: A boss the player has UNTICKED in Content Settings does not appear on their schedule at all. So a
capture reflects that player's filters, not the game's roster -- an absent boss may be filtered
rather than not scheduled. This roster was read with Boss and Archboss ticked and Boonstone
unticked, which is why the boonstone entries are named but never seen in a schedule capture.
